correctness.rationale: For each 1≤k≤N−1, direct selection of a distinct voter and two distinct other panelists yields birth a_k=k(N−k)[k−1+2p(N−k−1)]/[N(N−1)(N−2)] and death b_k=k(N−k)(N−k−1)/[N(N−1)(N−2)]. The finite harmonic equation forces differences Δ_(j+1)=w_jΔ_1; b_(N−1)=0 gives boundary saturation H(N−1)=H(N)=1. At p=1/2, w_j=(N−2)_j/(N−2)^j, exactly the survival tail of the first-repeated-label time for N−2 uniformly sampled labels. Tail-sum identities give the normalized truncated expectation for all boundary counts, including N=3. For moving p=1/2+λ/√N and k/√N→x, a uniform finite-window log expansion plus a global Gaussian envelope proves Riemann-sum convergence to F_λ(x)=∫_0^x exp(−t²/2−2λt)dt/∫_0^∞ exp(−t²/2−2λt)dt, and one-seed prefactor 1/I_λ. Independent checker enumerated microscopic triples in 81 finite (N,p,k) cases, independently checked harmonic recurrences and six exact birthday laws.

originality.rationale: Exact birth–death hitting formulas and the birthday-paradox survival law are standard mathematical ingredients. Muslim–NQZ–Khalif (2023) introduced/studied the exact media q-voter mechanism and supplied Fokker–Planck/continuum exit probability approximations and finite-size scaling (approximately 1/2). Their equations (14)–(15) are a diffusion ODE/integral, not a proof of exact finite microscopic absorption or a simultaneous λ-shifted √N seed/media limit. No inspected primary or published Resultary record proves the exact birthday identity or rigorous joint critical crossover; analogy with an existing diffusion scaling remains a priority risk, not a novelty proof.

Continuum Eq. (15) may heuristically encode the critical profile, but has not been established as an exact discrete implication.
